title: 2D nanobeam photonic crystal cavity, H_z eigenfrequency (FDFD)
description:
A 1D photonic crystal cavity in 2D: a 500 nm wide strip in air (eps_eff 8.12 = n 2.85, the TE effective index of a 220 nm silicon slab at 1550 nm) with a row of 12 air holes on each side of the centre (lattice a = 350 nm, r = 0.28 a). The two hole rows are Bragg mirrors for the guided mode; the centre-to-centre gap L_def between the two innermost holes is the defect: L_def = 1.5 a adds half a period, a quarter-wave phase shift, which puts the localised resonance near the middle of the mirror stop band. Solved by the eigenfrequency study in em_fdfd_hz (E in the plane: the TE-like nanobeam mode, E_y across the beam) near the target wavelength, with subpixel smoothing on the hole edges and CPML on all sides. The cavity mode leaks through the mirrors along the beam and scatters out of the beam into the air (in-plane radiation), both absorbed by the PML.
The target lambda_target = 2 a n_B, n_B = 2.05 from a first run, sits on the cavity mode (~1435 nm, Q ~6e3-9e3 for L_def = 1.43-1.5 a, PML share ~2e-4); with the first guess n_B = 2.2 (1540 nm) the nearest rows were the dielectric band-edge mode (~1620 nm, Q ~240, two bright lobes over the mirrors) and a leaky mode (~1523 nm, Q ~31, one-sided), and the cavity only showed up as Q_max. If a change moves the cavity off the target, the high-Q row of the resonance table (Q_max) is the cavity: set lambda_target to its wavelength (the PML stretch and materials are frozen at the target).
Sweep tab: lambda_1, Q_1 and Q_max vs L_def (1.3-1.7 a): the resonance tunes through the stop band (longer cavity, longer wavelength) and Q peaks near mid-gap.
Mesh: auto, 40 points per wavelength in each material (lambda_target / (40 n): 12.6 nm in the beam, which spans the whole length, 36 nm in the air, graded by 1.15), ~1.3e5 unknowns. Eigen solver node 'eigen_solver': GPU cuDSS (gpu backend, needs nvmath-python; 'GPU cuDSS, mixed precision' also works, 'Host SuperLU' without a GPU). The cavity mode is E mirror-odd about the beam axis (y = Ly/2) and about the cavity centre (H_z even about both; the quarter model found it with antisymmetric planes, not with a symmetric one at the centre); the full beam also holds the modes of the other parities, which crowd the target, so nanobeam_cavity_quarter_fdfd keeps only the cavity's parity with two mirror planes (a quarter of the unknowns); em3d/nanobeam_cavity_eighth_3d is the 3D eighth model.
Field tab: |H_z| and Re H_z of each resonance (Snapshot slider).

parameters.name: eps_beam
parameters.description: beam permittivity (effective index 2.85 of a 220 nm silicon slab, TE)

parameters.name: L_def
parameters.description: centre-to-centre spacing of the two innermost holes (the defect; swept)

parameters.name: margin
parameters.description: air beside the beam, and beam beyond the outermost hole + a, before the PML (the beam runs into the x PML)

parameters.name: L_mirror
parameters.description: innermost to outermost hole centre of one mirror (12 holes)

parameters.name: x_first
parameters.description: x of the innermost hole on the right (mirror image on the left)

parameters.name: n_bragg
parameters.description: Bloch index at the stop band, from a first run: cavity mode at ~1435 nm (sets the target only)

parameters.name: lambda_target
parameters.description: eigenfrequency target (1435 nm, on the cavity mode)
